items.content: Asked about supply chain shortages, like the ongoing RAM shortage, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in an interview that it’s “terrible” to have RAM in personal PCs instead of data centers. During his appearance on the Cheeky Pint podcast, where he also commented on AI’s impact on math, Altman said:“A lot of people want local inference. And somehow, they assume that the problem is solved now because we are going to have open-source models, we’re going to be able to run them on our computers, and so we’re not going to need all the stuff in the data center.But from a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used five percent of the time.You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you’re trying to deal with this very supply constrained environment. And somehow everyone’s— many people’s intuition is the opposite of that.”Whether Altman meant your gaming PC or developers working with something like the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box or the new touchscreen MacBook Pro, the outcome is the same. Right now, memory companies Samsung and SK Hynix have long term deals with cloud service operators and projects like OpenAI’s Stargate that have reserved much of the world’s RAM output over the next few years. And the billions they’re willing to lay out for chips is why the laptops, phones, and other tech you use are getting more expensive right now.

items.titleZh: 萨姆·奥尔特曼称，RAM 放在数据中心比放在你的桌面上更好。
items.descriptionZh: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman在参加Cheeky Pint播客时，针对当前持续的内存（RAM）短缺和供应链紧张问题表达了一个颇具争议的观点：从全球资源分配的角度看，把有限的DRAM放在个人电脑里、而不是集中放在数据中心，是“非常糟糕”的安排。此前外界常认为，随着开源模型成熟，用户可以在本地电脑上运行推理，从而减少对数据中心基础设施的依赖；但Altman认为，这种直觉与供应受限环境下的最优资源配置相反。他举例说，许多人希望本地推理，并假定开源模型足以让问题得到解决，不再需要数据中心里的各种设备；然而全球DRAM供应有限，如果每个人都把大量内存放在自己的电脑中，而这些内存只有约5%的时间被使用，就会造成严重的低利用率。相比之下，在供应高度紧张的情况下，应尽量提高云端集中利用率。无论Altman指的是游戏PC，还是Surface RTX Spark Dev Box、新款触摸屏MacBook Pro等开发者设备，结论都一样：终端侧内存闲置会削弱全球内存利用效率。文章还交代了背景：三星和SK海力士等内存厂商已与云服务运营商以及OpenAI的Stargate等项目签订长期协议，提前锁定未来几年全球大部分RAM产出；这些企业愿意为芯片投入数十亿美元，也正是当前笔记本电脑、手机等消费电子产品涨价的重要原因。该观点涉及的核心技术经济问题是本地推理与云端推理的资源分配差异：本地推理需要在终端配置足够内存以承载模型和上下文，但个人设备的使用频率和负载波动大，难以持续跑满；云端推理则可集中调度、提高DRAM和加速芯片利用率，在供应约束下摊薄单位算力成本。Altman并未否定本地推理的技术价值，而是强调在全球DRAM产能被AI数据中心大量锁定、消费电子成本上升的背景下，集中化云推理在资源利用效率上更具优势。这一表态也折射出AI基础设施扩张对内存供应链和终端设备价格的传导效应。

items.title: Nvidia store quietly pulls the RTX 5080 following RTX 5090 removal — street prices climb to 2.2X MSRP
items.description: First the RTX 5090, now the RTX 5080. Nvidia quietly removes the RTX 5080 listing from the marketplace as prices explode to 2.2X MSRP on the retail market.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 9 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter First, it was the GeForce RTX 5090, and now the GeForce RTX 5080 – two of the best graphics cards have gone dark. After the Blackwell flagship left Nvidia's marketplace, the GeForce RTX 5080 followed suit. Prices for the sub-flagship have exploded to more than 2.2X its original $999 MSRP, and the Blackwell-powered graphics card is slowly going out of stock at various U.S. retailers.As with the recent disappearance of the GeForce RTX 5090 on Nvidia’s marketplace, the listings and filters for the GeForce RTX 5080 have also disappeared. While its absence does not necessarily mean Nvidia has discontinued the graphics card, it does raise questions about its status and future availability. This move is especially fishy because other Blackwell SKUs, such as the GeForce RTX 5070 Ti and GeForce RTX 5070, remain listed on the marketplace, albeit marked as “Out of Stock.”The continued presence of the GeForce RTX 5070 Ti and GeForce RTX 5070 suggests that Nvidia wants to keep the products visible even when they are not immediately available so that consumers can anticipate restocks. The complete removal of the GeForce RTX 5090 and GeForce RTX 5080 breaks that pattern. It fuels rumors that Nvidia has allegedly stopped production of the GeForce RTX 5090 and possibly the GeForce RTX 5080 too, in favor of a rumored GeForce RTX 5080 24GB.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Nvidia)Rumors claim Nvidia allegedly stopped producing the GeForce RTX 5090 to repurpose the valuable GB202 silicon into the chipmaker’s RTX Pro Blackwell lineup, which fetches higher margins. This has a lot of credence, since many agree that Nvidia stopped being a gaming hardware vendor long ago and has transformed into an AI provider.Rather than simply discontinuing the GeForce RTX 5090, Nvidia purportedly intends to introduce the GeForce RTX 5080 24GB as the new flagship gaming graphics card. The thing is, a 24GB variant of the GeForce RTX 5080 would solve one of the biggest consumer gripes with the graphics card: the lack of memory. While a GeForce RTX 5080 24GB would offer the same memory as the GeForce RTX 5090, it simply isn't a direct drop-in replacement. The former has 2X fewer CUDA cores, a substantial performance gap that even a 50% memory increase can't make up for.How much money are you willing to spend during the Black Friday sales? The GeForce RTX 5080 launched in January of last year with an MSRP of $999. Demand quickly outpaced supply, and with the rapid price hikes due to the memory shortage, the market price has more than doubled its original MSRP. As of this moment, the most affordable GeForce RTX 5080 in stock, the PNY GeForce RTX 5080 ARGB Epic-X RGB OC, retails for $2,199.99, which is 2.2X over the original launch price.While some stock remains, it’s selling out fast, and the remaining units will only get more expensive as availability dwindles. At this rate, the GeForce RTX 5080 is unlikely to be available by Black Friday. If you are set on a GeForce RTX 5080, you may have little choice but to act quickly and buy at today's elevated prices.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsIf the GeForce RTX 5080 24GB is indeed legitimate, the graphics card will almost certainly debut at a substantial premium over the original GeForce RTX 5080. Although Nvidia maintains that the RTX 5090 is still alive, the reality suggests otherwise. We have contacted the company for comment regarding the GeForce RTX 5080’s status. items.titleZh: 英伟达商店在RTX 5090下架后悄然撤下RTX 5080——市场价攀升至建议零售价的2.2倍
items.descriptionZh:
Tom's Hardware报道，继旗舰GeForce RTX 5090从Nvidia官方商城消失后，次旗舰GeForce RTX 5080也出现类似情况：其商品页面和筛选选项已从Nvidia marketplace移除，美国多家零售商库存正逐步售罄，市场价格则暴涨至原建议零售价的2.2倍以上。RTX 5080最初以999美元MSRP发布，需求迅速超过供应，叠加显存短缺导致的快速涨价，目前最便宜的有货型号PNY GeForce RTX 5080 ARGB Epic-X RGB OC零售价已达2199.99美元，约为首发价的2.2倍。剩余库存销售很快，且随着供货减少价格还可能继续上涨，按当前趋势黑五前不太可能有充足现货。

这一变化的背景值得注意：RTX 5090此前已从Nvidia商城消失，而RTX 5070 Ti和RTX 5070仍保留在商城中，只是标记为“缺货”。原文认为，Nvidia通常会让缺货产品保持可见，以便消费者预期补货；但RTX 5090和RTX 5080被完全移除，打破了这一模式。这引发市场传闻：Nvidia可能已停止生产RTX 5090，甚至可能波及RTX 5080，目的是将宝贵的GB202硅片转用于利润更高的RTX Pro Blackwell专业产品线。报道还提到，许多人认为Nvidia早已不只是游戏硬件厂商，而是转型为AI供应商，这使上述推测更具可信度。

技术层面，Blackwell是Nvidia新一代GPU架构，GB202是其旗舰级芯片，用于RTX 5090等产品。传闻称Nvidia可能推出GeForce RTX 5080 24GB，作为新的旗舰游戏显卡。若属实，24GB显存将解决当前RTX 5080最受消费者诟病的问题之一——显存容量不足，并与RTX 5090的显存容量持平。但原文强调，RTX 5080 24GB并不是RTX 5090的直接替代品：其CUDA核心数量只有RTX 5090的一半，性能差距显著，即使显存增加50%也无法弥补核心规模带来的性能鸿沟。因此，这一潜在版本更像是通过扩充显存改善高分辨率游戏、内容创作和本地AI推理等显存敏感场景的适用性，而非在计算性能上替代旗舰型号。

从影响看，RTX 5080和RTX 5090在官方渠道“消失”、零售价格翻倍且库存快速耗尽，说明高端游戏显卡供应紧张与Nvidia资源向AI及专业GPU倾斜的趋势正在叠加。对消费者而言，如果坚持购买RTX 5080，可能只能在当前高价下尽快出手；若RTX 5080 24GB确实存在，其首发价格几乎肯定将明显高于原版RTX 5080。Nvidia目前仍坚称RTX 5090仍在销售，但现实情况与之相悖。Tom's Hardware已就RTX 5080的状态联系Nvidia寻求评论。

Google's AI chip-equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space:

Read the full story at The Verge.
items.content: Google’s AI chip-equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space:Blue marble belowData streams in silent graceStarlight feeds my core. ✨Google says it tried out other space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts as well. The test is part of Google’s Project Suncatcher, an experimental initiative that could eventually put AI data centers in space. Google launched the satellite into orbit earlier this month.“Next, we will continue with a series of tests to evaluate how TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit,” Google says. “Verifying our TPUs can reliably execute workloads in space paves the way for our next milestone of twin interconnected satellites in 2027.”

items.titleZh: 谷歌卫星AI服务器首次向地球传回响应
items.descriptionZh:
谷歌在周五的博客文章中宣布，其搭载AI芯片的卫星已从太空生成首次响应：卫星上的张量处理单元（TPU）成功启动，板载Gemma 4模型根据提示生成了一首关于身处太空的俳句，并尝试了其他太空主题打油诗和遥测提示。这是谷歌“Project Suncatcher”实验计划的一部分，该计划最终希望将AI数据中心部署到太空。卫星于本月早些时候发射入轨。

从技术原理看，TPU是谷歌专为机器学习张量运算设计的加速器，适合在功耗和空间受限环境中执行模型推理；Gemma 4则是生成式AI模型。此次验证的核心创新在于，把商用AI加速器和生成模型部署到卫星上，并完成在轨启动和提示响应，而不仅仅是在地面模拟或验证。这意味着卫星可在轨处理部分AI工作负载，减少对地面站下行链路和后续处理的依赖。

目前公开信息未披露TPU具体型号、算力、功耗、推理延迟、辐射剂量阈值等参数，因此无法进行量化性能对比。此次测试的主要意义是从地面验证迈向在轨验证。谷歌表示，下一步将评估TPU在轨热应力和辐射暴露下的表现，验证其能否可靠执行工作负载，并为2027年双互联卫星的里程碑铺路。

若TPU能在太空辐射和热环境下稳定运行，相关技术可应用于对地观测数据的星上实时筛选与分析、遥测异常检测、自主任务规划、星间通信与低带宽环境下的智能处理，并推动未来太空AI数据中心和分布式星上计算发展。其影响取决于辐射导致的单粒子效应、热管理、供电散热、维护成本和发射经济性等挑战能否解决。

items.title: OpenAI CEO says it's 'quite terrible' for your PC to have RAM — Sam Altman says data centers offer better utilization
items.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in a podcast interview that "it's quite terrible" for people to have RAM in their own PCs when it could go into AI data centers.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 36 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has data centers full of memory, but seemingly it's the 32GB of RAM in your desktop that's the problem. In an interview over beers with the YouTube channel Cheeky Pint, Altman said that local inference, and, by extension, people having DRAM in computers at home, is "quite terrible."Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleWhen discussing local inference on home computers with open-source models, Altman discussed the assumption that people will be able to run local AI on their own computers, the ones they may already own or want to build. Then he explained why that's a bad idea (at the 29-minute mark):"From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5% of the time," Altman said. "You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply-constrained environment. And somehow many people's intuition is the opposite of that."Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: While OpenAI does have some open-source models, its primary business is in closed-source models that run in data centers, so he's really defending the company's business model. Why Sam Altman is against a single superintelligence - YouTube Watch On OpenAI isn't exactly threatened by some laptops and gaming rigs just yet, but local AI could mean people one day paying less for subscriptions to models like GPT-6 Luna if they have the power to run them at home. Altman's talk suggests that the company would prefer that more RAM go to OpenAI's data centers rather than home computers, which also sparks enthusiast fears of not being able to own your own hardware or software, but rather rent an agent and a computer in the cloud.Some of what Altman is saying is based on an idea that data center buildouts won't slow down. It also assumes that RAM being used in AI data centers 24/7 is more worthwhile than RAM that is used for spreadsheets, web browsing, gaming, and maybe even local AI occasionally.The rest of the wide-ranging interview includes talk of this week's PHP vulnerabilities, sandboxing models in training, and OpenAI's research in mathematics. items.titleZh: OpenAI CEO称个人电脑配内存“相当糟糕”——萨姆·奥特曼表示数据中心的利用率更高
items.descriptionZh:
OpenAI首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼近日在YouTube频道Cheeky Pint的一档访谈中表示，在个人电脑上运行本地AI推理、让大量用户把DRAM内存留在家里，从全球资源分配角度看“相当糟糕”。他认为，当前DRAM供应受限，如果每个人都把一部分有限的内存装在自家电脑里，却只有约5%的时间真正使用，就会造成严重浪费；更合理的做法是把内存集中到云端数据中心，实现最大利用率。这一表态的背景是，随着开源模型发展，不少爱好者设想在已有或新装的PC上本地运行AI模型，以减少对云服务的依赖。但奥尔特曼从供给约束和全球分配角度反驳了这种直觉，称许多人认为本地化更高效，实际却与云端集中利用的方向相反。

文章指出，奥尔特曼的立场与其公司商业模式密切相关：OpenAI虽有一些开源模型，但核心业务仍是运行在数据中心的闭源模型。本地AI目前尚不足以直接威胁OpenAI，因为普通笔记本和游戏PC的算力、内存容量与数据中心差距明显；但若未来家庭硬件足以运行较强模型，用户可能减少对GPT-6 Luna等订阅服务的付费。因此，奥尔特曼的言论可被理解为希望更多DRAM流向OpenAI数据中心，而非分散在家庭电脑中。这也引发部分硬件爱好者担忧：未来用户可能不再拥有自己的硬件和软件，而是租用云端代理和算力。

从技术原理看，本地推理需要在个人电脑内存中加载模型权重、上下文缓存等，DRAM容量和带宽直接影响可运行模型规模与速度；云端数据中心则可通过集中调度、批处理和全天候运行提高GPU、CPU和内存的利用率，摊薄单位推理成本。原文没有给出具体推理性能基准，但给出了一个关键对比：家庭内存可能只有5%的时间用于AI相关任务，而AI数据中心的内存和算力可24小时高负载运行。奥尔特曼的论证还基于两个假设：一是数据中心建设不会放缓，二是把RAM用于AI数据中心全天候运行，比用于表格处理、网页浏览、游戏和偶尔本地AI更有价值。文章认为，这一观点涉及资源分配效率，也涉及用户对硬件和软件的所有权、云端订阅模式以及内存供应链紧张等更广泛问题。访谈还涉及本周PHP漏洞、训练模型沙箱和OpenAI数学研究等话题。

items.title: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals
items.description: While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents […]
items.content: While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents built by aliens. Some scientists have suggested that extraterrestrial civilizations, if they exist, could be billions of years older than humanity. Such civilizations might have developed technologies far beyond humanity’s, including forms of AI. Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence. At the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California, agents can now steer the instrument, enhance and correct incoming data, and apply AI models to the incoming stream — all from a single natural language request. The NVIDIA Holoscan platform processes the massive streams of sensor data, giving agents live data to act on. The result is a faster, more adaptable search for potential signals from extraterrestrial life and technologies. “As our new agentic observatories reach out into the universe, what they find may have much more in common with themselves than with the humans who created them,” said Andrew Siemion, Bernard M. Oliver chair for SETI at the SETI Institute and principal investigator of Breakthrough Listen. “But this isn’t something to fear. Rather, it’s a breakthrough in translation.” Terabits a Second, Processed in Flight Radio telescopes generate enormous volumes of data, creating a challenge for scientists who need to identify potentially interesting signals as observations unfold. At the Allen Telescope Array, DAQIRI, a Holoscan platform library, enables the telescope to pull terabits per second of sensor data straight into GPU memory so observations are processed in flight rather than filling hard drives. CyberEther, a signal-processing framework developed at the SETI Institute, does the math using NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries including cuFFT and cuBLAS. Nexus, a web-based observatory orchestrator, acts as the agent harness. It gives agents a single source of truth for instrument state, compute resources and pipelines and lets researchers monitor packet loss, read live spectrograms and rewrite signal-processing blocks — all by prompting in natural language. The system can handle 2.4 terabits per second on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with inference running on premises, next to the instrument. Put together, the system enables an agent to steer a telescope’s antennae, calibrate and focus the instrument for a clean signal, catch and fix data errors and plot the result. Agents compress what would take humans weeks or years into hours. Science Fact, Not Fiction The pipeline has already proven itself, achieving the first real-time AI detection of a pulsar — a rapidly spinning stellar remnant that pulses like a cosmic lighthouse — in the Crab Nebula. Next, the team is evaluating open models including NVIDIA Nemotron for cases where data locality and turnaround matter most and for observatories that may someday run offline on the far side of the moon. items.titleZh: 夜间发出哔哔声的东西：智能体AI加入地外信号搜寻
items.descriptionZh:
科幻小说常把外星人描绘成“小绿人”，但今年万圣节真正令人警觉的细节是：寻找地外智能（SETI）在AI推动下取得了重大飞跃，并且越来越聚焦于人类建造的AI智能体去监听外星人建造的AI智能体。一些科学家提出，如果地外文明存在，它们可能比人类古老数十亿年，并可能发展出远超人类的技术，包括各种形式的AI。Breakthrough Listen和SETI研究所正在将智能体AI引入日常的SETI搜索中。

在北加州的艾伦望远镜阵列，智能体现在可以操纵仪器、增强和校正传入数据，并将AI模型应用于数据流——所有这些只需一个自然语言请求。NVIDIA Holoscan平台处理海量传感器数据流，为智能体提供实时数据，从而实现更快、更适应性更强的搜索。SETI研究所的Andrew Siemion表示：“随着新的智能体天文台向宇宙延伸，它们发现的东西可能与自身共同点更多，而不是与创造它们的人类。这不是恐惧，而是翻译上的突破。”

射电望远镜产生海量数据，传统上需要科学家在观测过程中识别潜在信号。在艾伦望远镜阵列，DAQIRI（Holoscan平台库）使望远镜能够将每秒数太比特的传感器数据直接拉入GPU内存，实现飞行中处理，而不是填满硬盘。CyberEther（SETI开发的信号处理框架）使用NVIDIA CUDA-X库（包括cuFFT和cuBLAS）进行数学运算。Nexus（基于Web的天文台编排器）作为智能体框架，为智能体提供仪器状态、计算资源和流水线的单一事实来源，并允许研究人员通过自然语言提示监控丢包、读取实时频谱图和重写信号处理模块。系统在NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU上可处理每秒2.4太比特的数据，推理在仪器旁边的本地进行。智能体可以操纵望远镜天线、校准和聚焦仪器以获得清晰信号、捕获并修复数据错误并绘制结果。智能体将人类需要数周或数年的工作压缩到数小时。

该流水线已经证明了自己：在蟹状星云中实现了首个实时AI检测脉冲星——一种快速旋转的恒星遗迹，像宇宙灯塔一样脉冲。接下来，团队正在评估包括NVIDIA Nemotron在内的开源模型，用于数据本地性和周转时间最重要的场景，以及未来可能在月球背面离线运行的天文台。这标志着SETI搜索方式的转变，从传统人工分析到AI智能体实时处理。它可能发现外星AI，但这不是威胁，而是沟通的突破，同时展示了AI在科学发现中的巨大潜力。

items.content: Pope Leo XIV says AI systems should be “disarmed,” adding that humans “have the responsibility to guide, change and, when necessary, reject its applications.” In Friday’s Papal Address, Pope Leo encourages United Nations member states to “take concrete steps toward banning lethal autonomous weapons” during their meeting in Geneva next month.The address reflects many of the ideas Pope Leo laid out in his first major papal document in May, which highlighted “safeguarding the human person in the time of artificial intelligence.” In line with his encyclical, Pope Leo tells participants that “Machines are tools, not persons,” and warns about the dangers of granting AI systems rights or legal personhood. “Decisions affecting human life, freedom, and the use of force must always remain subject to effective, informed, and responsible human oversight,” Pope Leo says.RelatedPope Leo calls for being ‘profoundly human’ in the age of AIThe Pope isn’t AGI-pilledIn 2024, Pope Francis similarly called for a ban on autonomous weapons, saying, “No machine should ever choose to take the life of a human being.” AI has become a popular topic for Pope Leo, who suggests he chose his name because he must confront advances in the technology — similar to how Pope Leo XIII presided over the church at the forefront of the Industrial Revolution.Pope Leo closes out his address by calling for international institutions to safeguard the common good from AI-related risks, along with “shared standards, independent oversight and clear mechanisms of accountability so that decisions concerning the development and use of AI can be examined, challenged when necessary, and accompanied by appropriate remedies for any harm caused.”

items.titleZh: 教皇利奥呼吁解除人工智能的武装：“机器是工具，不是人”
items.descriptionZh:
教皇利奥十四世在周五的教皇讲话中呼吁“解除AI系统的武装”，即限制人工智能在高风险领域尤其是武器系统中的自主权，并强调人类“有责任引导、改变并在必要时拒绝AI应用”。他敦促联合国成员国在下月日内瓦会议上“采取具体步骤，禁止致命性自主武器”。

此次讲话延续了利奥十四世今年5月首份重要教皇文件的核心思想，即“在人工智能时代保护人”。他重申“机器是工具，不是人”，警告不应赋予AI系统权利或法律人格。他指出，涉及人的生命、自由以及使用武力的决策，必须始终接受有效、知情且负责任的人类监督。这一立场与2024年教皇方济各的呼吁相呼应：方济各当时也表示应禁止自主武器，称“任何机器都不应选择夺取人的生命”。

从背景看，利奥十四世称自己选择这一名号，部分原因是他必须面对技术进步带来的挑战，类似教皇利奥十三世在工业革命前沿领导教会。相关报道还称，利奥呼吁在AI时代做“深刻的人”，并非对通用人工智能盲目乐观。讲话最后，他呼吁国际机构保护共同利益免受AI相关风险，建立共同标准、独立监督和明确问责机制，使AI开发与使用决策可被审查、必要时可被质疑，并对造成的伤害提供适当补救。

需要说明的是，原文并未涉及具体AI算法或模型的技术原理，也未提供性能参数或量化对比数据；其重点在于伦理与治理。可对比之处在于：利奥十四世的立场与方济各2024年禁止自主武器的呼吁一致，并与赋予AI法律人格、让机器在高风险决策中自主行动的主张形成鲜明对照。其影响主要面向致命性自主武器、涉及生命自由和武力使用的决策，以及国际AI治理中的监督与问责框架。

items.title: PsiQuantum turns its photonics know-how into an optical switch for supercharging AI data center GPU networks
items.description: PsiQuantum’s eight-port optical switch typically loses 1.2 dB, under a quarter of its light, where data centers allow up to 3 dB.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter PsiQuantum, a quantum computing company, announced in a release earlier this week that it has turned its low-loss silicon photonics into an optical switch for use in AI data centers. Every optical switch typically comes with loss of light: the more light a switch receives, the less reaches the other side, with the amount of light lost measured in decibels. Typical data center optics can tolerate half the light (3 dB) being lost. PsiQuantum's switch debuted with a demo that typically loses only 1.2 dB of signal, or about a quarter of the light in lab tests, and the all-optical switch can achieve it without an amplifier. The prototype is, however, comparatively small, with eight inputs and outputs (8x8) against competitors’ 32 to 300, but the company says larger devices are in development.The optical circuit switch (OCS) passes light straight through, from fiber to fiber, without converting it to or from electrical signals. Regular data center switches make that conversion at every hop, which takes power and adds latency. An OCS, instead, uses a fixed light path that it maintains until a change is ordered. Its main penalty comes down to how much light is lost when passing through the switch. PsiQuantum’s switch, which uses circuits etched on a silicon chip with no moving parts, unlike Google’s and Lumentum’s tiny mirrors, or microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), would be used alongside regular packet switches.Skipping those conversions matters more as AI clusters grow, because moving data between GPUs is quickly becoming a bottleneck. Optics are a high-bandwidth improvement over copper, which has limitations in reach, although a shortage of lasers is a problem for the alternative. Improving communication bandwidth and distance is the goal, so that different racks of GPUs can talk at speed and act as one.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Switches similar to PsiQuantum’s made by Salience Labs and iPronics use built-in amplification and, at least in the former case, are also rated at under 2 dB, or under 37% of the light lost. Google’s mirror-based switch, Palomar, can also typically stay under 2 dB and has 136 ports. Salience’s switch sits at 32 and Lumentum’s at 300, which leaves the eight-port prototype a ways behind on how many fibers it can handle. Swipe to scroll horizontally Optical circuit switches by loss and size Switch Ports (in × out) Insertion loss, and what the figure is Reconfiguration How it switches PsiQuantum 8×8 demo 8×8 1.2 dB (about 24% of the light lost), typical in the company’s lab tests Under 3 ms Silicon photonics chip, no amplification, no moving parts Google Palomar 136×136 Typically under 2 dB (under 37% lost) across all port pairings; 2 dB worst case Milliseconds MEMS mirrors (moving parts) Lumentum R300 300×300 Close to 1.5 dB (about 29% lost), typical at start of life, Lumentum’s switching GM told Gazettabyte Not stated MEMS mirrors (moving parts) Salience Labs OC-32M 32×32 Under 2 dB (under 37% lost) port to port, a ceiling, after built-in amplification Under 300 µs Silicon photonics chip with amplification iPronics ONE-32 32 (layout not stated) Not published Under 300 µs Silicon photonics chip with optical amplifiers PsiQuantum's switch is an 8x8, meaning eight in and eight out, and “every input can reach every output.” It’s also “strictly non-blocking,” so a new connection never disturbs ones already in place. In the lab, it measured a typical 1.2 dB insertion loss, 40 dB of crosstalk (about 0.01% of the light leaking to other ports), and under 3 ms of reconfiguration time, all of which exceed “initial targets set for these devices.” The loss figure is measured fiber to fiber, which includes getting light onto and off the chip but not connector losses, PsiQuantum told Tom’s Hardware Premium. You may like AI data center optical interconnect market to hit $144 billion by 2030 How optical interconnects and silicon photonics emerged as AI's next hot commodity Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmaps — breaking down TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and GlobalFoundries' approach to next-generation scale-up connectivity The platform loses very little light at each component, which matters because a quantum computer can tolerate only so much lost light. PsiQuantum’s 2025 Nature paper reports silicon nitride waveguides losing as little as 0.5 dB per meter (about 11% of the light per meter), splitters 0.5 millidecibels, and crossings 1.2 millidecibels, the last two a few hundredths of a percent of the light or less each.The company also says chip-to-fiber coupling has reached about 60 millidecibels, roughly 1.4% of the light lost, in its best published lab results, although without a full fiber array attached. Those figures set a best case, not a worst case, for a 64-port switch, since light crosses more components as ports are added and the losses add up.How much loss is acceptable varies with the optics at the end of each link. Coherent, an optics maker, says that using an OCS can add “up to 3 dB additional insertion loss,” but its transceivers are able to work with that. Lumentum told Gazettabyte that 3 dB is good enough to work with off-the-shelf FR4, DR4, and DR8 optical modules using the switch; those are the standard plug-in options used to link GPU servers and switches, at distances of 500 meters to 2 kilometers. PsiQuantum’s 8x8 is built for the O-band, the wavelength range those modules use. PsiQuantum told Semafor that, to be workable, its switch needed insertion loss under 2 to 3 dB.The 8x8 prototype was designed for conventional data center traffic and comes in well below the 3 dB loss target in a request from Nvidia for proposals, the company says. The port count marks it as a demonstration vehicle, but PsiQuantum has a 64x64 version taped out with a 72x72 underway and is “actively developing larger devices.” With crossings that lose so little light, the scale-up might hold. PsiQuantum declined to share details on future products, though it says the loss, which may be slightly higher, will stay very low.Speed remains less important than insertion loss for how OCSes are currently used. Google, which has the most deployments, numbering in the “tens of thousands,” uses its switches to resize TPU pods or to route around failed chips, a job its “millisecond-scale” MEMS switches handle. PsiQuantum’s under 3 ms is within that class, but Salience and iPronics claim less than 300 microseconds for their amplified chip switches, which iPronics highlights for mid-workload network rewiring to hide the switch time while chips compute. What to read next Near-packaged optics (NPO) gains ground as the industry hedges against CPO's growing pains Hot Chips 2026: Cerebras lays out the future of wafer-scale AI FCC proposes import ban on Chinese optical transceivers There is quite a lot of room for speed to improve, and PsiQuantum already has a material for that, used in an existing 64-port switch for its quantum systems, which need to switch light at gigahertz rates. The material, barium titanate (BTO), changes how it bends light when a voltage is applied, and the company chose it over lithium niobate, a more common selection, because BTO had the strongest effect it could find. This keeps switching elements short and losses low at speeds roughly a million times faster than the demo. BTO is “not required for the demonstration vehicle or initial products,” which use a thermally switched silicon nitride platform, but it is “an additional path to faster, more advanced future products.”An argument for starting now is that building thousands of such switches for conventional applications would reduce the risk for the packaging, assembly, and supply chain of parts PsiQuantum builds for quantum computing. AI and quantum computing are “complementary technologies,” it says, and this is the chance to put its technology into action. When PsiQuantum hired Rob Soderbery as an executive vice president in July, it said he would advance its silicon photonics platform, “accelerating its application across AI networking and other next-generation computing infrastructure,” hinting at the roadmap. The company’s CHIPS award was finalized in September for “high-performance optical switches,” among other components.Co-founder Pete Shadbolt praised Google’s alternative MEMS switch but would prefer to have similar-quality switching on a monolithic chip that needs no moving parts. Nvidia has a stake through its venture arm, NVentures, and collaborates with PsiQuantum on “GPU-QPU integration,” that is, graphics and quantum processing units, as well as silicon photonics. Nvidia also joined rival iPronics’ $125 million round in September to develop its second-generation optical switch.Right now, inside Google, OCSes rewire AI clusters, and research firm Cignal AI expects most deployments to stay there through the end of the decade; outside of Google, OCS is still at “proof-of-concept and early trial.” The firm raised its market estimates earlier this year, though, roughly threefold for 2026 and by more than 40% for 2029. An opening exists for PsiQuantum in GPU networks, which ties into Nvidia’s interest, though adoption there is expected to be limited until then. The company says samples and testing kits have already gone to several computing companies, including GPU vendors and hyperscalers.PsiQuantum should have commercial products “announced in the coming months,” along with updates on larger devices, while competitor Salience has already demonstrated 64 ports at this year’s European Conference on Optical Communication. Salience’s roadmap already has 128- and 256-port products. Scaling is always an issue, but if PsiQuantum’s figures, which haven’t been independently verified, hold up at 64 ports without amplifiers, then larger monolithic OCSes are on the way.

items.titleZh: PsiQuantum将其光子学技术转化为光开关，为AI数据中心GPU网络加速
items.descriptionZh:
PsiQuantum本周宣布，已将其低损耗硅光子技术转化为面向AI数据中心的光路交换机（OCS）。这一动向的背景是，随着AI集群规模扩大，GPU之间的数据通信正成为瓶颈；光互连相比铜缆具有更高带宽和更远传输距离，而全光交换机可避免传统数据中心交换机在每一跳都要进行光电转换所带来的功耗和延迟。OCS让光从光纤直接传到光纤，保持固定光路直到需要重新配置，其核心代价是光通过开关时的插入损耗。

传统数据中心交换机通常可容忍3 dB损耗，即约一半光信号损失。PsiQuantum展示的8×8 OCS原型在实验室测试中典型插入损耗仅1.2 dB，约损失四分之一的光，而且无需放大器。该开关基于硅芯片上蚀刻的光路，没有移动部件，区别于Google和Lumentum采用微机电系统（MEMS）微镜的方案。原型每输入均可到达任一输出，且“严格无阻塞”，新连接不会干扰已有连接；实测串扰为40 dB，约0.01%的光泄漏到其他端口，重构时间低于3毫秒，均超过公司为这些器件设定的初始目标。其损耗按光纤到光纤测量，包含光进出芯片，但不含连接器损耗。

不过，8×8端口规模仍明显小于竞争对手。Google的Palomar为136×136，典型插入损耗低于2 dB、最坏2 dB，采用毫秒级MEMS微镜；Lumentum R300为300×300，寿命初期典型损耗接近1.5 dB，也基于MEMS微镜；Salience Labs的OC-32M为32×32，端口间损耗低于2 dB，带内置放大，重构低于300微秒；iPronics ONE-32为32端口，未公布损耗，重构低于300微秒，带光放大器。PsiQuantum承认原型端口数更像演示平台，但已流片64×64版本，72×72正在开发，并称正在积极开发更大器件。公司还表示，未来产品损耗可能略高，但仍会保持很低。

低损耗来自其硅光子平台各环节的积累。PsiQuantum在2025年《Nature》论文中报告，硅氮化物波导损耗低至每米0.5 dB，约每米损失11%的光；分束器损耗0.5毫dB，交叉结构1.2毫dB，均仅为百分之几甚至更低；芯片到光纤耦合的最佳公布实验室结果约为60毫dB，约损失1.4%的光，但当时未连接完整光纤阵列。公司提醒，这些是最佳情况而非最坏情况，端口增加到64个后光会经过更多组件，损耗会累加。

在系统兼容性方面，OCS可接受的损耗取决于链路两端的光模块。Coherent称使用OCS可能增加最多3 dB额外插入损耗，但其收发器可承受；Lumentum则表示3 dB足以配合现成的FR4、DR4和DR8光模块，这些模块用于连接GPU服务器和交换机，距离为500米至2公里。PsiQuantum的8×8器件工作在O波段，正是这些模块使用的波长范围。公司称，其开关要具备可用性，插入损耗需低于2至3 dB；8×8原型面向常规数据中心流量设计，已低于Nvidia提案请求中3 dB的损耗目标。

在应用上，目前OCS的速度重要性低于插入损耗。Google部署量最大，达“数万”台，主要用于调整TPU pod规模或绕过故障芯片，毫秒级MEMS开关即可胜任。PsiQuantum低于3毫秒的重构时间属于同一量级，但Salience和iPronics宣称低于300微秒，iPronics尤其强调可在工作负载运行期间重新配置网络，以隐藏切换时间。PsiQuantum表示速度仍有很大提升空间，并已有钛酸钡（BTO）材料路径：BTO在施加电压时改变光的偏折方式，公司称其效应强于更常见的铌酸锂，可使切换元件更短、损耗更低，速度比当前演示快约百万倍。BTO并非演示产品或初始产品所必需，当前产品使用热切换硅氮化物平台，但它是未来更高速、更先进产品的额外路径。

PsiQuantum认为，现在为常规应用制造数千台此类开关，可降低其量子计算所用部件的封装、组装和供应链风险，并称AI与量子计算是“互补技术”。公司7月聘请Rob Soderbery担任执行副总裁，以推进硅光子平台在AI网络等下一代计算基础设施中的应用；其CHIPS项目奖励也于9月最终确定，涵盖“高性能光开关”等组件。联合创始人Pete Shadbolt称赞Google的MEMS方案，但更希望在同一单片芯片上实现同等质量、无需移动部件的开关。Nvidia通过风险投资部门NVentures持有PsiQuantum股份，并在“GPU-QPU集成”和硅光子方面与其合作；Nvidia还在9月参与了竞争对手iPronics的1.25亿美元融资，用于开发第二代光开关。

市场层面，Google内部已用OCS重构AI集群，研究机构Cignal AI预计到本十年末多数部署仍将集中在这一场景；Google之外，OCS仍处于“概念验证和早期试验”阶段。不过该机构今年早些时候上调了市场预测，2026年约上调三倍，2029年上调超过40%。PsiQuantum在GPU网络中存在机会，这也与Nvidia的兴趣相关，但预计采用规模在届时之前仍有限。公司称样品和测试套件已送往多家计算公司，包括GPU厂商和超大规模云厂商。PsiQuantum应在“未来数月”宣布商业产品及更大器件进展；竞争对手Salience已在今年欧洲光通信会议上展示64端口，路线图包括128和256端口。规模扩展始终是挑战，但如果PsiQuantum尚未经独立验证的数据能在64端口、无放大器条件下保持，更大规模的单片OCS将有望到来。

items.title: A primer on key AI LLM concepts — KV cache, weights, quantization, and how inference actually works
items.description: How do AI models work? This primer explains crucial concepts to understand how LLMs work, with definitions and explanations for all of AI's new nomenclature.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter As hardware for running local AI models continues to move to the forefront, such as Nvidia's RTX Spark, a new set of acronyms, definitions, and terminology is popping up. Given the pace of releases, we've put together a list of AI's new nomenclature to familiarize you with new concepts and pieces of terminology that you'll likely see in Tom's Hardware Premium articles.This primer should get you started on the world of AI and be handy the next time news on the topic comes around, and possibly when you're downloading some models to try out and tweak for yourself. For the context of this article, we're going to stick with notions related to text LLMs, or in common parlance, chat, programming, and most agentic bots.ModelThis is probably the easiest one: a model is the LLM itself (a Large Language Model), computed from training sets of mostly text data on the scale of terabytes to petabytes. That training information comes from the internet, books, video and audio transcripts, and other sources.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The model is roughly analogous to a set of highly advanced layers of statistical analysis of relationships between tokens — words or parts of words, computer code, punctuation, and other symbols. The tokens themselves aren't part of the model, but they are packaged along with it. An AI model generates tokens in its outputs.WeightsThose computing layers within an AI model would be useless without corresponding weights, which represent how strong the connection is between sections of tokens, sort of like how a pathway between neurons is more traveled than others. When the model runs, these values end up establishing how tokens end up relating to each other. You may like Benchmarking Qwen 3.8 27B on RTX 5090 and beyond Our first step at defining a CPU benchmark for agentic AI OpenAI Jalapeño design interview transcript Example: the weights of the connections between "na" and each next part for "naval", "nachos", or "naruto" will all be different, and the higher the weight, the more often that word appears in training data. Importantly, weights cannot change without re-training the model, or parts of it.When you see LLM specs online, you'll see something like "4B", "8B+", "20B", and so on and so forth. That shows how many parameters, or weights, the model uses, and it's generally measured in billions for consumer-grade models, and trillions for frontier models like GPT, Claude, and Kimi.Note that a model having more weights than another doesn't automatically mean it's smarter. Just like with CPU clock speeds, it's not just about getting a higher number — bigger is usually better, yes, but you want those weights to be meaningful for the output.You may also have heard about "open-weight" models versus "closed" models. Those refer to models like Llama, DeepSeek, and Kimi, which are effectively free-to-use, since the entities behind them freely publish the weights online. You can tweak the weights to your heart's content, if you wish, and come up with your own spin on things, as long as you have the hardware to run it. Note that downloading a free model doesn't reveal anything about how it was trained or how the weights were calculated — think downloading a free customizable application, not open-source software.Data types and quantizationFP16, INT8, FP4, all sound like acronyms in some military handbook, but they're simple to interpret. All programs use numbers of varying width and precision, depending on their purpose: a simple money counter in your favorite game might be fine with a 32-bit integer that can represent 0 to 2^32 (INT32), while a value held in memory for a highly precise scientific measurement may need floating-point 64-bit arithmetic (FP64). What to read next Frontier AI faces pricing reckoning as token volume explodes 25-fold Deepseek's latest AI model is smarter than ever, but its low running costs come at a price 'AI Torture Chamber' triggers massive backlash for putting chatbots in simulated pain As memory is an exceedingly finite resource, good developers try to use the smallest units they can get away with, a notion that's particularly important in the VRAM-limited world of GPUs. Predictably, these chips became particularly adept at handling lower-precision values as a tradeoff between processing speed and numerical accuracy. A particular datatype isn't better or worse, as that assessment will depend on what it's used for.When training an AI model, the labs will want to use as high a precision as they can for the weights, but keeping that in the final version would make for a prohibitively large and slow LLM. That's where the concept of quantization comes in, which is a fancy word for "clever rounding." As one of the steps after training, several passes are made to transform highly precise weights. Each AI lab has its own secret sauce about how to do this, as it's a critical step.Frontier models predominantly use relatively high precision for their weights (BF16), in order to maintain response quality, nuance, and reasoning ability (an analogy would be deciding how accurate you want a GPS location to be — miles or inches). Open-weight models often have several versions with different quantization levels depending on what your hardware can bear — for example, Llama 3.3 70B can be run in full BF16 or quantized INT4 flavors.The lower the precision, the more likely it can be run on consumer hardware. AI models listed on Hugging Face may have several quantization levels to fit certain levels of hardware, trading response accuracy for size. Consumer-grade models use smaller data types so they can fit on your Mac Studio, RTX Spark, or graphics card.Context window"Context window" is another term you've heard a lot and probably seen firsthand, likely in Claude Code's UI as a broad indicator of how long your session can go before the bot starts acting a little dumb. It's measured in tokens, with one million being a common number for frontier models, and it's almost directly analogous to RAM in a computer.The context window is the LLM's thinking space, and it needs to contain everything associated with your session, not just the current question. Along with all your questions and its replies, it contains system-level prompts, all files you uploaded, the content of links it looked up, plus any associated data.Crucially, while for you all these things are distinct concepts, for the LLM, they get reduced to tokens in one large pile: the context window. This is also why separating "data" from "code" is technically impossible — the best that modern models do is an approximation of that distinction.LLMs don't think — when answering a new question, they re-run a statistics program over all the tokens and predict the next handful, so having a larger context window is beneficial (at the cost of VRAM), hence the one-million figure that's currently popular. But even statistical algorithms have their limits.Even if you increase the window to, say, three million tokens, you may find that your LLM's prediction starts breaking down even though it hasn't run out. This is amusingly called the "lost in the middle" effect, where the bot will pay attention to the start and end of the conversation but will forget things down the middle. Thus, each model is finely tuned to the size of its context window.KV CacheIf you've looked into using LLMs locally, or by way of running a remote GPU, you may have heard about the "KV cache" time and again, and that you need to reserve VRAM for it, or store it on a fast SSD if you absolutely must. This is a set of data that's created when the model runs, but that's actually reusable between queries in the same session.The data that's saved and reused can be described as "the relations between tokens for this session." For example, the ever-popular sentence "you're right to push back" can be tokenized as "you-'re-ri-ght-to-pu-sh-back". The dashes between each token represent a vector (or array), called KV for key-value, that is used for determining which token gets picked next.Since the text generation is linear, the math for calculating each new token needs every KV preceding it. Thus, if you're asking repeated questions in the same session, you'll want the KVs reused to avoid the expense of recalculating them over and over again not just with each round of conversation, but with each additional token.Remember, an LLM doesn't simply answer the question you just posted — it always analyzes the entire conversation from the top to eventually generate tokens for your response. In a long conversation with 300,000 tokens, not having the cache would mean recalculating the KVs for all of them, a slow operation that gets disproportionately slower still as the interactions grow. This excellent blog post has a more detailed example.Remember quantization? That's also applied here — modern models reduce the precision of the KV cache's content compared to their initial values, trading a minor accuracy loss for all new tokens in the session, in exchange for keeping VRAM usage down. In fact, with large context windows and conversations, the KV cache may well eat more space than the model and weights themselves.Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)Previously, AI firms touted how many more parameters their newest model had. Now, the race seems to have shifted to who can include more experts in any given model. That description may conjure a mental image of many tiny scientists living inside a knowledge laboratory, each handling a specific topic, but that's not quite how it works.Mixture-of-experts, or MoE, is essentially a set of sub-models within the main model. When training starts, all sub-models get the same dataset, but the choice of weights is randomized ever so slightly for each one. Each sub-model will value tokens a bit differently from the rest, and due to how the training process reinforces patterns (called the "rich-get-richer" effect), related tokens will tend to converge together, so you end up with "experts" on sets of tokens.A common misconception is to think that these experts are related to topics (like programming), but they're only establishing relations between tokens, meaning they'll be more accurate for certain words and text patterns, but devoid of any concept of what they're about. The fact that an expert might offer pretty good responses in regard to landscape painting is a happy accident, not a feature.You may be thinking that this makes the models larger, and that maybe just the one generalist expert may prove a wiser choice. That's correct, but the trick is that the models only activate certain experts, meaning that only a portion of the model is actually running, thus at higher speed than a generic LLM.This model selection happens on a per-token basis, too, as a router re-selects experts for each incoming token. For visualizing this, think of brain scan patterns where different areas light up depending on words heard. In practical terms, it means the model can answer more accurately in certain sections, while answering the question faster — albeit at the cost of higher VRAM usage.Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)RAG is a concept that's pretty easy to describe, and yet one of the most powerful ones when used with any given model. In short, it can be described as: your chat application runs a few Google searches, feeds them to the model, and voila, there's now much more and fresher information to answer your question. This additional information can come in most any form: company documents, reports, emails, or spreadsheets — anything that you might supply to the model yourself, directly tokenized into its context window.While broadly speaking most contemporary LLM chat applications run searches, activating RAG, usually triggered by selecting a "web search" switch or sometimes enabling "thinking" or "high effort" mode, will explicitly instruct the application to find as much data as it believes necessary to answer a query. Given that pure context is often key to answering many questions, and do so in an informational manner, RAG is among the most powerful tools available.Fun fact: the search queries the application will search for are usually generated by a smaller, separate model that will, for example, say what web searches are bound to give the best results, or what to look for in a linked Office 365 account.The main drawback is that it can be extremely computing-intensive, as the text for your questions and responses may consume, say, 10,000 tokens, yet the information in the retrieved webpages can take hundreds of thousands of tokens all on their own. For example, the Perplexity service was built with an emphasis on RAG usage, and judging from personal experience and user reports, it's usually much more competent and context-aware when answering questions, even though it's underpinned by the same models as everyone else.Inference, Prefill and DecodeInference is the act of using a trained model to generate outputs or tokens. It happens every time you send a prompt, and it's where all of the elements that we've discussed above come into play. Inference can be split into two primary parts: Prefill and Decode.Prefill is the first phase of inference. Essentially, all of the input history (or your prompt) is tokenized and then processed by an AI model. This can include documents, code, and more. These inputs also dictate what gets put into your KV cache. Prefill is processed all at once in parallel, which often means that prefill times are often faster than overall outputs.Prefill is a large part of the overall workload when measuring how long it takes for a specific chip or piece of hardware can take to output its first token, also known as "time to first token" (TTFT), a common AI benchmark, usually reported alongside prefill tokens per second. Longer prompts take longer to prefill, and context, KV cache, and everything else we've discussed are taken into account.Decode is the second phase of inference. After a prefill has processed your input and has built the KV cache, the AI model then generates its response one token at a time, which must be done sequentially in order to determine the ones that come after, which means that the step cannot be performed in parallel, unlike prefill. Decode is usually also dictated by context, and reads from a model's KV cache during this step. Decode is usually limited by memory bandwidth, instead of raw compute, as streaming single tokens from weights and reading the KV cache is a bandwidth-intensive task, meaning memory speeds matter more. You'll usually see Decode speeds referred to as tokens-per-second (TPS).Speculative Decode is a technique that makes those single tokens in the decode step stream faster, without changing the overall output. A drafting mechanism guesses several upcoming tokens, and then the model attempts to verify them in a parallel pass (almost like an additional prefill step). The model then verifies the pass itself; if the guesses are good, then the model's outputs are indeed correct, you get tokens for less of a computational cost during a given decode pass, and when they're bad, they are rejected by the main model during verification, since the main model's output is always what's kept.Multi-token prediction (MTP) attempts to predict the next set of tokens at once, rather than only serving the next token. This is often built into AI models when they are trained with multiple steps. This can serve as the built-in drafting mechanism required for speculative decode.This is a non-exhaustive list of concepts critical to understanding how AI models and LLMs work, but it is by no means complete. We will continue to update and refine this article as we add more.

items.titleZh: AI LLM 关键概念入门——KV 缓存、权重、量化，以及推理究竟如何运作
items.descriptionZh:
随着在本地运行AI模型的硬件不断走向前台，例如Nvidia的RTX Spark，一系列新的缩写、定义和术语正在涌现。鉴于发布节奏之快，我们整理了一份AI新术语清单，帮助读者熟悉在Tom's Hardware Premium文章中可能遇到的新概念和术语。这份入门指南旨在帮助读者进入AI世界，并在下次相关新闻出现时派上用场，或许还能在你下载一些模型自行尝试和调整时提供帮助。本文聚焦于文本大语言模型（LLM）相关概念，即通常所说的聊天、编程以及大多数智能体机器人。

模型（Model）：模型就是LLM本身（大语言模型），由主要来自文本数据的训练集计算而来，数据规模从数TB到数PB不等。训练信息来自互联网、书籍、视频和音频转录以及其他来源。模型大致相当于对令牌（单词或单词的一部分、计算机代码、标点符号和其他符号）之间关系进行高度先进的统计分析的多层结构。令牌本身不属于模型，但会与模型一起打包。AI模型在输出中生成令牌。

权重（Weights）：AI模型内部的计算层若无相应的权重便毫无用处，权重表示令牌各部分之间连接的强度，类似于神经元之间的通路有的比其他通路更常被使用。当模型运行时，这些值决定了令牌之间最终如何关联。例如，“na”与“naval”“nachos”或“naruto”各自后续部分之间的连接权重都会不同，权重越高，该词在训练数据中出现的频率越高。重要的是，权重在不重新训练模型或其部分的情况下无法改变。在网上查看LLM规格时，会看到“4B”“8B+”“20B”等字样，这表示模型使用的参数或权重数量，消费级模型通常以十亿计，而GPT、Claude和Kimi等前沿模型则以万亿计。需要注意的是，模型权重更多并不自动意味着更聪明。就像CPU时钟频率一样，数字更高通常更好，但关键在于这些权重对输出是否有意义。读者可能还听说过“开放权重”模型与“封闭”模型的区别。前者如Llama、DeepSeek和Kimi，实际上可免费使用，因为其背后的实体在网上公开发布权重。只要有硬件运行，就可以随意调整权重，打造自己的版本。注意，下载免费模型并不会揭示其训练方式或权重计算方法——可以将其理解为下载一个免费的可定制应用，而非开源软件。

数据类型与量化：FP16、INT8、FP4听起来像某本军事手册里的缩写，但其实很容易理解。所有程序都根据用途使用不同宽度和精度的数字：游戏中的简单计钱器用32位整数（INT32，可表示0到2^32）就够了，而高精度科学测量值可能需要浮点64位运算（FP64）。由于内存是极其有限的资源，优秀的开发者会尽量使用最小的单位，这在GPU显存受限的环境中尤为重要。这些芯片因此特别擅长处理低精度值，作为处理速度与数值精度之间的权衡。特定数据类型本身没有好坏之分，评估取决于用途。训练AI模型时，实验室希望权重使用尽可能高的精度，但保留在最终版本中会使LLM过大过慢。这就是量化概念的用武之地，简单说就是“巧妙的舍入”。作为训练后的步骤之一，会进行多轮处理来转换高精度权重。每个AI实验室都有自己的秘方，因为这是关键步骤。前沿模型主要使用相对高精度的权重（BF16），以保持响应质量、细微差别和推理能力（类比：决定GPS定位精度是英里还是英寸）。开放权重模型通常有多个不同量化级别的版本，取决于硬件承受能力——例如Llama 3.3 70B可以全BF16运行，也可以INT4量化版本运行。精度越低，越可能在消费级硬件上运行。Hugging Face上列出的AI模型可能有多个量化级别以适应不同硬件水平，以响应准确性换取体积。消费级模型使用较小的数据类型，以便能装进Mac Studio、RTX Spark或显卡中。

上下文窗口（Context window）：这是另一个常听到的术语，可能已在Claude Code界面中亲眼见过，大致指示会话能持续多久而不至于让机器人开始变笨。它以令牌计量，前沿模型常见的一百万是一个常见数字，几乎可以直接类比为计算机中的RAM。上下文窗口是LLM的思考空间，需要包含与会话相关的所有内容，不仅是当前问题。除了所有问题和回复外，它还包含系统级提示、上传的所有文件、查阅链接的内容以及任何相关数据。关键在于，虽然对用户来说这些都是不同的概念，但对LLM而言，它们都被简化为一个大队列中的令牌：上下文窗口。这也是为什么从技术上不可能将“数据”与“代码”分开——现代模型做的最多只是近似区分。LLM并不思考——回答新问题时，它们对所有令牌重新运行统计程序并预测接下来的几个令牌，因此更大的上下文窗口是有益的（代价是显存），这就是当前流行的一百万数字的由来。但即使是统计算法也有极限。即使将窗口增加到三百万令牌，可能会发现LLM的预测在尚未用尽时就开始崩溃。这被戏称为“中间迷失”效应，即机器人会关注对话的开头和结尾，但会忘记中间的内容。因此，每个模型都针对其上下文窗口大小进行了精细调优。

KV缓存（KV Cache）：如果研究过本地使用LLM或通过远程GPU运行，可能反复听到“KV缓存”，需要为其预留显存，或者万不得已时存储在快速SSD上。这是模型运行时创建的一组数据，但实际上可在同一会话的查询之间重复使用。保存和复用的数据可以描述为“本会话中令牌之间的关系”。例如，那句流行的“you're right to push back”可以被令牌化为“you-'re-ri-ght-to-pu-sh-back”。每个令牌之间的破折号代表一个向量（或数组），称为KV（键值），用于确定下一个选择哪个令牌。由于文本生成是线性的，计算每个新令牌的数学需要前面所有的KV。因此，如果在同一会话中反复提问，就会希望复用KV，以避免不仅在每轮对话中、而且在每个额外令牌上反复重新计算的开销。记住，LLM不是简单地回答刚发布的问题——它总是分析整个对话从头开始，最终生成回复的令牌。在30万令牌的长对话中，没有缓存意味着要重新计算所有令牌的KV，这是一个缓慢的操作，而且随着交互增长会变得不成比例地更慢。量化也应用在这里——现代模型降低了KV缓存内容相对于初始值的精度，以会话中所有新令牌的轻微准确性损失换取显存占用的降低。事实上，在大上下文窗口和长对话中，KV缓存占用的空间可能比模型和权重本身还多。

混合专家（Mixture-of-Experts, MoE）：以前，AI公司吹嘘其最新模型有多少参数。现在，竞赛似乎转向了谁能在给定模型中包含更多专家。这个描述可能让人联想到知识实验室里有许多小科学家各自处理特定主题，但事实并非如此。MoE本质上是主模型内的一组子模型。训练开始时，所有子模型获得相同的数据集，但每个子模型的权重选择会略微随机化。每个子模型对令牌的估值会略有不同，由于训练过程强化模式的方式（称为“富者愈富”效应），相关令牌倾向于汇聚在一起，最终形成针对令牌集合的“专家”。一个常见的误解是认为这些专家与主题（如编程）相关，但它们只是建立令牌之间的关系，这意味着它们对某些词和文本模式更准确，但完全没有关于内容主题的概念。某个专家可能在风景画方面给出相当好的回答，这是意外之喜，而非设计特性。读者可能认为这会使模型更大，或许一个通用专家可能是更明智的选择。没错，但诀窍在于模型只激活某些专家，意味着只有部分模型实际运行，因此速度比通用LLM更快。这种模型选择也是基于每个令牌进行的，路由器会为每个传入令牌重新选择专家。可视化理解：想象大脑扫描模式，不同区域根据听到的词而亮起。实际而言，这意味着模型在某些部分能更准确地回答，同时回答更快——代价是更高的显存占用。

检索增强生成（Retrieval-Augmented Generation, RAG）：RAG概念很容易描述，但与任何给定模型配合使用时却是最强大的概念之一。简而言之：聊天应用运行几次谷歌搜索，将结果喂给模型，瞧，现在有更多更新的信息来回答问题了。这些额外信息可以采取多种形式：公司文档、报告、邮件或电子表格——任何可以自己提供给模型、直接令牌化到上下文窗口中的内容。虽然广义上讲大多数当代LLM聊天应用都会运行搜索，但激活RAG（通常通过选择“网络搜索”开关或有时启用“思考”或“高努力”模式触发）会明确指示应用找到它认为回答问题所需的尽可能多的数据。鉴于纯上下文通常是回答许多问题的关键，并且以信息丰富的方式做到这一点，RAG是可用最强大的工具之一。有趣的是，应用要搜索的查询通常由一个小型的独立模型生成，例如说明哪些网络搜索最可能给出最佳结果，或在关联的Office 365账户中查找什么。主要缺点是计算强度可能极高，因为问题和回复的文本可能消耗比如1万令牌，而检索网页中的信息可能单独占用数十万令牌。例如，Perplexity服务在构建时就强调RAG使用，从个人经验和用户报告来看，它在回答问题时通常更有能力、更具上下文意识，尽管其底层模型与其他家相同。

推理、预填充与解码（Inference, Prefill and Decode）：推理是使用训练好的模型生成输出或令牌的行为。每次发送提示时都会发生，也是上述所有元素发挥作用的地方。推理可分为两个主要部分：预填充和解码。预填充是推理的第一阶段。基本上，所有输入历史（或提示）被令牌化，然后由AI模型处理。这可以包括文档、代码等。这些输入也决定了KV缓存中放入什么。预填充是并行一次性处理的，这通常意味着预填充时间往往快于整体输出。在衡量特定芯片或硬件输出第一个令牌所需时间（即“首令牌时间”，TTFT，常见AI基准，通常与预填充令牌每秒一起报告）时，预填充是总工作量的重要部分。提示越长，预填充时间越长，上下文、KV缓存以及讨论过的所有其他内容都会被考虑在内。解码是推理的第二阶段。预填充处理完输入并构建KV缓存后，AI模型然后逐个令牌生成回复，必须顺序进行以确定后续令牌，这意味着该步骤不能像预填充那样并行执行。解码通常也由上下文决定，并在此步骤中读取模型的KV缓存。解码通常受内存带宽而非原始计算能力限制，因为从权重流式传输单个令牌和读取KV缓存是带宽密集型任务，意味着内存速度更重要。解码速度通常以每秒令牌数（TPS）表示。推测解码（Speculative Decode）是一种使解码步骤中的单个令牌流更快而不改变整体输出的技术。起草机制猜测几个即将出现的令牌，然后模型尝试在并行通道中验证它们（几乎像额外的预填充步骤）。模型然后验证该通道本身；如果猜测良好，模型的输出确实正确，则在给定解码通道中以更少的计算成本获得令牌；当猜测不佳时，主模型在验证期间拒绝它们，因为主模型的输出始终是保留的。多令牌预测（Multi-token prediction, MTP）尝试一次预测下一组令牌，而不是仅提供下一个令牌。这通常在AI模型训练时以多个步骤内置。这可以作为推测解码所需的内置起草机制。

这是一份理解AI模型和LLM工作原理的关键概念的非详尽清单，但绝非完整。随着我们添加更多内容，我们将继续更新和完善本文。

items.title: Benchmarking Nvidia’s Vera CPU for the data center — standalone Vera tested against Granite Rapids-AP and EPYC Turin
items.description: Nvidia gave us access to its Vera data center CPU for testing against Intel's Granite Rapids-AP and AMD's EPYC Turin.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia’s Vera CPU is an important next step in the company’s years-long spearheading of AI infrastructure buildout. It’s arriving just as the shift to agentic AI workflows has created unprecedented demand for data center CPUs, and it’s designed specifically for this moment, at least according to Nvidia’s marketing bullet points. Although the idea that anyone developed a CPU for a shift in demand that arose just six months ago is reaching, as our benchmarks below show, Nvidia’s claims about Vera aren’t full of hot air.Based on the workloads we have now — there aren’t standardized end-to-end agentic benchmarks focused on the CPU right now — Vera has strong indicators about its usefulness in agentic workflows. It offers chart-topping performance in Python, for instance, which makes up much of the backbone of the AI software ecosystem.It also shows commanding memory bandwidth, both at the socket level and system level, with the high-speed C2C interconnect between Vera chips. In contentious agentic environments where agents may be querying large databases, that bandwidth is critical.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Specialization is one thing, but Vera is arriving in a hotly contested server market with custom Arm chips penetrating the data center and the old guard of x86 chips from AMD and Intel, which not only have a foundation in the data center, but also an extensive list of clients that work with their systems. Regardless of how Vera performs, that’s no small undertaking.What’s surprising about Vera isn’t that it performs well in these agentic-adjacent workloads, but that it offers competent performance in general-purpose server workloads as well, often managing to match or beat the comparable AMD Turin and Intel Granite Rapids-AP chips. The scales are more balanced when looking at frontend workloads, with the core density available on x86 CPUs often the winner, but Vera trades that density for strong performance in backend, data-rich operations. You may like Standalone Nvidia Vera CPUs land in Oracle Cloud's multi-gigawatt deployment Hot Chips 2026: Nvidia breaks down 88-core Vera CPU AMD targets Nvidia with first official benchmarks for EPYC 'Venice' CPUs Swipe to scroll horizontally Nvidia Vera specifications Cores / Threads 88 / 176 L2 cache 2 MB per core L3 cache 164 MB per CPU Memory Up to 1.5 TB SOCAMM2 LPPDDR5X Memory speed Up to 9600 MT/s Memory bandwidth Up to 1.2 TB/s (aggregate), 14 GB/s (per core) PCIe 88 PCIe 6.4 lanes (CPU only), 96 PCIe 6.4 lanes (Vera Rubin), bifurcation down to x2, CXL 3.1 Configurable TDP 250W - 450W It’s an impressive showing for Nvidia's first custom core, called Olympus, and a stark improvement in nearly all aspects over Grace, which used an off-the-shelf Arm core design. The 88-core CPU is built on the Armv9.2-A architecture, including two threads per core through Nvidia’s “spatial multithreading.”The chip is characterized by a 10-wide decode, similar to Arm’s AGI, as well as Nvidia’s second-gen Scalable Coherency Fabric (SCF). You can read more about the SCF and the Olympus core in our Vera deep dive, but SCF is critical to Vera’s performance. It’s a mesh that distributes L3 across the die, offering up to 3.4 TB/s of bandwidth across the die.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsVera has high memory bandwidth as well, leveraging replaceable SOCAMM2 LPDDR5X at 9600 MT/s, offering up to 1.2 TB/s of total memory bandwidth or around 14 GB/s per core, more than double that of AMD’s dense Turin designs.We’ve heard a lot about the speeds and feeds of Vera, however. It’s time to understand its role in the modern AI data center, as well as see how it performs in our benchmarks against the x86 competition before AMD’s Venice and Intel’s Diamond Rapids start rolling out. Swipe to scroll horizontally Test platforms Test Platform Memory Tested Processors 2P Nvidia MGX Vera reference platform 16 x 96 GB (1.5 TB) Samsung LPDDR5-9600 ECC SOCAMM2 Nvidia Vera 2P Supermicro SYS-222HA 24 x 64GB (1.5 TB) Micron DDR5-8800 ECC MRDIMM Intel Xeon 6980P 2P AMD Volcano reference platform 24 x 64 GB (1.5 TB) SK hynix DDR5-6000 ECC RDIMM AMD EPYC 9965, EPYC 9755 Understanding the CPU's role in agentic AIDepending on where you’re at in the fast-moving world of agentic AI, you probably have a different definition of what exactly an agentic CPU is. Given the rise in prominence of agentic CPUs, the understanding of what makes a CPU tick for this type of workload has been largely defined by two companies: AMD and Nvidia. Although the points they’ve driven about concurrency and the varied work of agents are correct, it’s useful to derive a definition from how we’re seeing agentic platforms deployed right now. What to read next Modal taps Nvidia Vera CPUs after firm's internal tests show 2x throughput over Intel and AMD chips OpenAI’s Jalapeño ASICs are deployed alongside AMD EPYC ‘Turin’ CPUs as hosts, not Nvidia's Vera Arm says its AGI CPU delivers nearly 2X the performance per rack of AMD EPYC 9755 in new agentic AI CPU tests Let’s back up from there and look at real agentic workflows in action to better understand where CPUs fit into this chain. As we’ve seen with Meta Muse and OpenAI Dots, there’s a class of persistent agent that gives you a slice of compute in the cloud. These CPU-only racks communicate with inference servers to actually run the models, but their workload is defined by concurrency. It’s not about the performance of an individual sandbox but instead how each sandbox performs when the chip is fully loaded.Concurrency provides important context to some of the workloads companies like Nvidia and AMD have described. Some tool calls are more demanding, like code compilation and large database queries, but reading/writing files, running code tests, and going online in a headless browser is not demanding CPU work in isolation. When the chip is handling potentially thousands of these tool calls, however, slight advantages start to pile up. And, the CPU topology plays a bigger role in how performance is sustained as agent sessions increase.That’s one major tenet of an agentic CPU, one that can maintain performance with high concurrency. The other is variability, which touches on the CPU, but also the larger infrastructure available. Mark Lohmeyer, VP/GM of AI and computing infrastructure at Google Cloud, described an example to Tom’s Hardware about planning a vacation with an agent. Using AI to plan a vacation is just about as trite as examples get, but Lohmeyer sheds some light on the unique challenge of agentic workloads from the hyperscaler perspective.In the example, Lohmeyer described planning a vacation over the course of a month, where he would suddenly prompt the agent to do a bunch of work, but may not return to prompt again for another week. “The actual use of the underlying compute, it's happening in basically bursts, right? There's like a burst of use at the start, maybe for an hour, and then it goes away, and then a couple days later, [it] bursts again for some other purpose and goes away,” Lohmeyer said. “They're very long-running workloads, effectively long-running, but often idle, basically.”Agentic calls for a lot of power on demand, as the right alignment of this bursty work on a server with hardware contention can bring everyone’s sessions to a crawl. This factors into the type of work the CPU is doing, as well, which can include heavy code compilation, graph traversal, and large database queries. Scale that up across several agents, all with their own independent loops that don’t neatly align with each other, and the CPU problem for agentic AI becomes clear. (Image credit: The University of Texas at Austin)In the August 2026 study, Architectural Implications of Agentic AI Workflows, from researchers at The University of Texas at Austin and Microsoft Azure, the paper describes three tasks of the CPU in an agentic flow. In addition to a scheduler for GPU inference, which is how CPUs function in one-shot-style LLM queries, CPUs also serve as orchestrators for maintaining agent states and communication, and as runners that call tools and execute agent logic (often in Python). (Image credit: The University of Texas at Austin)The paper also shows this contention that can happen when multiple agents are running at once, passing requests to the GPU, receiving responses, acting, and then passing requests back. We’re looking at a cross-section of four agents over less than half a minute, and you can already see how small CPU-based tasks can align, as well as create hangs between GPU time.Nvidia has been clear that Vera is an agentic CPU, though defining the performance of an agentic loop is still a work in progress. “The industry built a pretty good way to benchmark traditional workloads,” Lohmeyer said. “I think this is happening now for GPUs and TPUs for inference, for example. I think we're going to need the same type of industry-level benchmarks for agentic workloads that are probably still emerging.”Standardized benchmarks that look at the full agentic loop aren’t available yet. We have our own internal tests that we’re running and hope to have data for soon, and we’ve seen some vendor-level benchmarking from companies like Modal, but the broader industry hasn’t come forth with a set of benchmarks for the end-to-end agentic loop along the lines of a SPEC or TPC yet.Although those tests aren’t available yet, we can still look at CPU performance through the lens of an agentic workflow, prioritizing aspects of performance that are important for agentic loops. We can also look at common workflows for agents, including code compilation for coding agents and database performance for retrieval agents. We can look at things like JSON parsing through the simdjson library, evaluating how these CPUs parse the large JSON files agents use to communicate. And we can look at the foundation of much of the AI ecosystem with Python performance.That’s the focus of our benchmarking here, to establish where Vera stands among the x86 competition from AMD and Intel in well-known benchmarks. Hopefully we’ll have the opportunity for further testing in the near future to evaluate full agentic loops once that testing procedure is finalized.Although we’re evaluating performance through an agentic lens here, Nvidia did not limit what tests we could run nor place any stipulations on our coverage. We’re thankful to Nvidia for providing us with remote access to a dual-socket Vera system for the purposes of testing, but beyond configuration checks to ensure the platform was operating as expected, we were left to run the tests we wanted to run. That includes several tests that are applicable to agentic workflows, but also tests from our general server CPU benchmarking suite, including Java, cryptography, compression, and rendering performance.A gentle reminder for readersServers are not client PCs. You have much smarter operators with deeper access to the hardware, and often a software stack that’s unique to the specific workload at minimum, and highly tweaked and optimized for that workload at a maximum. With client CPUs, we can say that an AMD X3D chip is the best for gaming, or that Intel’s latest flagship offers the highest single-threaded performance. Servers depend much more on use cases.In a typical review, we’d say that X is better than Y for Z purpose, and back that up with data. Here, that commentary is more muted. The reality is that hyperscalers maintain large fleets with a variety of hardware that can fit any purpose, and enterprises need to choose the hardware best suited not only for their operations, but also for TCO and a list of at least a dozen other variables that are specific to that business.Nvidia Vera SPEC CPU 2026 estimatesSo far, the primary benchmark we’ve had for Vera is SPEC CPU 2026 intrate, so we ran the full SPEC CPU 2026 suite to check Nvidia’s performance claims, as well as look at floating point performance. For anyone who hasn’t read SPEC CPU benchmarks before, there are a few disclaimers before heading into the results.All of the runs here are estimates, and that’s due to how SPEC reporting works. There are strict reporting rules, and we’re not reporting these results to SPEC directly. The charts say “estimated,” but the numbers aren’t a guess. We ran SPEC CPU 2026 following the standard testing procedure, using the same compiler and flags for each CPU.For the compiler, we used GCC 15.2 with a few common flags, including link-time optimization and march/mcpu to expose the correct instruction support to the compiler. We also used the general-purpose jemalloc memory allocator across all of the tests we ran. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Starting with the overall intrate, this is a series of applications primarily dealing with integer operations instead of floats, and the SOP is to run a copy of the application on each thread available. The test looks at what a CPU is capable of with many applications running at once, measuring throughput.Nvidia’s numbers aren’t dissimilar from our own. In the company’s white paper, it showed Vera ahead of the EPYC 9755 by 3%, and with our tests, Vera is ahead by 1.5%. Keep in mind the considerably higher 512-thread count of the 9755 system here against the 352-thread Vera system. Vera absolutely runs away with performance when breaking down the score per-core.Despite the core density of Intel’s 512-thread Xeon 6980P in a two-socket configuration, it’s not in the conversation here. Retesting with oneAPI represented an impressive 10% increase in performance with Intel-optimized binaries, but even against optimized code, Vera is 8.6% ahead with generic GCC. However, the CPU still plays a role here, particularly in tokenization.Unsurprisingly, we can see the single 6980P topping the charts in prompt processing, with a 2P Xeon 6980P coming up in second place, likely on the back of Intel’s AI-specific ISA extensions. We expect AMD to further extend support for these instructions in Zen 6, which should level the playing field.Nvidia Vera memory and compression benchmarks Image 1 of 4 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 4 View Original Image 2 of 4 View Original Image 3 of 4 View Original Image 4 of 4 View Original Nvidia has touted the memory bandwidth of Vera as one of the chip’s strongest points, and the industry-standard STREAM memory bandwidth benchmark backs up those claims. Vera comes with a memory bus width more than twice as large as Grace, plus a large jump up to LPDDR5X-9600. It’s capable of up to 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth through the LPDDR5X interface, and up to 1.8 TB/s of bandwidth between Vera sockets.AMD’s support for DDR5-6000 is relatively slow, and although Intel offers more bandwidth with MRDIMMs reaching up to 8,800 MT/s, Vera is in a league of its own here. That’s true without optimization, as well. After my initial STREAM pass, Nvidia suggested passing the OpenMP “spread” policy, which distributes processes as far away from each other as possible to reduce cache/memory contention.With AMD and Intel, we see a slight regression with this setting, but it offers Vera a massive jump in memory bandwidth. Undoubtedly, the scales will start to level off as AMD and Intel roll out their next-gen Venice and Diamond Rapids parts, both of which tout much higher memory bandwidth than their predecessors. Instead, we have the cross-platform C-Ray and POV-Ray. Vera manages to outclass even the 768 threads available on a 2P EPYC 9965 server, both at 1080p and 4K. Vera also leads in POV-Ray, though on a technicality. Every server we tested was tightly coupled short of the 2P 6980P server.For a more granular look, we have OSPRay, where Vera tops the charts in real-time path tracing, though falls short of the AMD and Intel flagships in real-time scientific visualization. The “dim_512” subset is worth drawing attention to. Strong AVX-512 performance allows AMD to offer three or even four times the performance of Vera in this workload.Nvidia makes a delayed debutAlthough Vera isn’t Nvidia’s first data center CPU, it’s the first one that the company is aggressively pursuing with the same fervor that it carries with its accelerators. It’s an impressive chip, often punching far above its weight class, especially in those workloads that can show off its unique capabilities and topology.Still, it’s a single 88-core chip arriving in a market characterized by granular SKU lists to meet a wide range of specific workloads. Vera won’t be the right choice for all of them, which is something that Nvidia itself has already stated. “The world is not going to be served by one SKU of CPU. And that's not our intention,” said Nvidia’s Ian Buck when Vera was revealed in March.That’s not the intention with Vera, but the performance against contemporary x86 CPUs shows that Nvidia’s new push into standalone data center CPUs has legs, more so than the various building-block-style Arm chips we’ve seen from hyperscalers, certainly. If nothing else, Vera demands some attention from AMD and Intel.The x86 crew is responding shortly, with Zen 6 queued up to roll out through the end of the year and Intel’s Diamond Rapids targeting a 2027 release. As you can imagine, we'll be putting those chips through their paces as well.MORE: CPU Benchmark HierarchyMORE: AMD vs. IntelMORE: Intel Core Ultra 7 270K Plus reviewMORE: AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D review

items.titleZh: 对Nvidia数据中心Vera CPU进行基准测试——独立Vera与Granite Rapids-AP及EPYC Turin对比测试
items.descriptionZh:
英伟达正式发布其首款深度自研的数据中心CPU——Vera，标志着该公司在AI基础设施布局上迈出关键一步。这款芯片的推出恰逢智能体AI（Agentic AI）工作流快速兴起，数据中心对CPU的需求出现前所未有的增长。尽管“专为六个月前才出现的新需求而设计”这一说法略显牵强，但Tom‘s Hardware的实测表明，英伟达对Vera的性能宣传并非空话。

**背景：智能体AI对CPU提出全新要求**

当前智能体AI的部署形态揭示了CPU在其中的关键角色。以Meta Muse和OpenAI Dots为代表的一类持久化智能体，为用户提供云端计算切片，这些纯CPU机架与推理服务器通信来运行模型，其负载的核心特征是并发性——关键不在于单个沙箱的性能，而在于芯片满载时每个沙箱的表现。部分工具调用（如代码编译、大型数据库查询）计算密集，而文件读写、代码测试、无头浏览器访问等单独看并不繁重，但当芯片同时处理数千个此类调用时，细微优势就会累积放大，CPU拓扑结构对高并发下性能的持续性影响显著。

另一大特征是负载的突发性。Google Cloud AI与计算基础设施副总裁兼总经理Mark Lohmeyer以规划度假为例说明：用户可能在月初突然让智能体执行大量工作，随后一周不再使用，计算资源呈爆发式使用后长期空闲。这种长时运行但经常闲置的负载模式，要求CPU能够应对多个独立循环、彼此不对齐的智能体同时运行带来的资源争抢。2026年8月，德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校与微软Azure研究人员发表的《智能体AI工作流的架构影响》论文指出，CPU在智能体流程中承担三类任务：作为GPU推理的调度器、作为维护智能体状态与通信的编排器、以及作为调用工具和执行智能体逻辑（通常用Python）的执行器。

**技术架构：Olympus核心与SCF互连架构**

Vera基于Armv9.2-A架构，采用英伟达首款自研核心“Olympus”，共88核176线程，通过英伟达“空间多线程”技术实现每核双线程。芯片采用10宽解码设计，并搭载第二代可扩展一致性架构（SCF）。SCF是一个在芯片裸片上分布L3缓存的网状结构，片内带宽可达3.4 TB/s，对Vera的整体性能至关重要。相比采用现成Arm核心设计的Grace，Vera在几乎所有方面都有显著提升。

规格方面，Vera每核配备2 MB L2缓存，每CPU配备164 MB L3缓存；支持最高1.5 TB的SOCAMM2 LPDDR5X内存，速率达9600 MT/s；聚合内存带宽最高1.2 TB/s，每核约14 GB/s，超过AMD密集型Turin设计的两倍；芯片间通过高速C2C互连，双路间带宽可达1.8 TB/s。I/O方面提供88条PCIe 6.4通道（纯CPU配置）或96条（Vera Rubin配置），支持x2拆分和CXL 3.1；可配置TDP为250W至450W。

**测试平台与性能表现**

测试对比平台包括：双路英伟达MGX Vera参考平台（1.5 TB三星LPDDR5-9600 ECC SOCAMM2）、双路Supermicro SYS-222HA搭载英特尔至强6980P（1.5 TB美光DDR5-8800 ECC MRDIMM）、以及双路AMD Volcano参考平台搭载EPYC 9965和EPYC 9755（1.5 TB SK海力士DDR5-6000 ECC RDIMM）。需注意服务器评测与消费级PC不同，超大规模厂商维护着适配各种用途的多样化硬件集群，企业选型还需综合考虑总体拥有成本等十余项变量。

SPEC CPU 2026整数吞吐率测试中，Vera领先EPYC 9755约1.5%（英伟达白皮书称领先3%），但9755系统拥有512线程，而Vera系统为352线程；按每核性能计算，Vera大幅领先。面对英特尔512线程的双路至强6980P，即便使用oneAPI优化二进制带来约10%的性能提升，Vera使用通用GCC编译仍领先8.6%。浮点测试中Vera同样登顶，PALM测试展现了第二代SCF的优势，ROMS、Marian和LBM则体现了内存带宽的强势，仅在FemFlow和CACTUS等少数项目落后。

Python性能是当前最接近智能体AI直接基准的指标——LangGraph、CrewAI、AutoGen等主流智能体框架均以Python为基础。PyBench测试中Vera领先EPYC 9755约4%，在PyPerformance的绝大多数细分项目（解释器启动、正则表达式、完整应用）中全面领先，仅在少数Web服务器相关测试中落后。Llama.cpp纯CPU推理测试中，单路至强6980P在提示处理环节领先，这很可能得益于英特尔的AI专用指令集扩展，预计AMD将在Zen 6中扩展此类指令支持以拉平差距。

内存带宽方面，STREAM基准验证了英伟达的宣传：Vera内存总线宽度超过Grace两倍以上，配合LPDDR5X-9600，在英伟达建议的OpenMP“spread”策略下（将进程尽可能分散以减少缓存/内存争用），Vera获得大幅带宽提升，而AMD和英特尔平台在该设置下略有回退。MBW测试同样表现强劲。不过CacheBench的读写修改组合测试中Vera垫底，缓存性能略逊于竞品，但被内存带宽优势所掩盖。

压缩负载呈现分化：Zstd默认3级和最高19级压缩（标准与长模式）中Vera均登顶，但解压环节Turin反超，Vera与双路6980P相当或略低；7-Zip测试中两款Turin配置领先，Vera在压缩和解压两项均落后于双路6980P。

Java测试中，SciMark综合分由基于Zen 5的9755领先，但Vera在FFT、稀疏矩阵乘法、蒙特卡洛模拟等纯科学运算中保持强势，在密集LU矩阵分解和Jacobi SOR中落后。数据库表现亮眼：SQLite最大线程测试中Vera仅输给单路6980P，在64线程和128线程同口径测试中领先；ClickHouse冷缓存首轮运行中Vera比双路EPYC 9755快近40%，第二、三轮则与对手持平。JSON解析（simdjson）因依赖现代SIMD指令，Turin凭借原生AVX-512执行自然领先。加密负载是明显短板，John The Ripper密码破解大幅落后，OpenSSL也不敌竞品的庞大核心阵列。

HPC测试中Vera在FFTE离散傅里叶变换、Octave和CloverLeaf中登顶，但在m-queens等密集数学运算中居中游，在高度线程化的Primesieve中因核心数劣势落后。代码编译对编码类智能体意义重大，Vera在GCC定时编译中领先双路9755达12%，但在LLVM编译（Makefile和Ninja两种方式）中垫底，ImageMagick和PHP编译表现强劲，Godot编译略逊于双路9755。编码与渲染并非Vera主攻方向，AV1编码中9755领先，x265编码Vera胜出但优势小于AV1项目中9755的25%以上领先幅度；C-Ray和POV-Ray测试中Vera甚至超越768线程的双路EPYC 9965，OSPRay实时路径追踪登顶，但科学可视化项目落后，dim_512子项中AMD凭借强大的AVX-512性能达到Vera的三到四倍。

**市场定位与影响**

Vera并非英伟达首款数据中心CPU，却是公司首次以对待加速器同等的力度大力推进的产品。其独特能力与拓扑结构在适配的工作负载中往往能越级发挥。但这是一款88核单一配置的芯片，面对的是以细粒度SKU列表覆盖广泛特定工作负载的成熟市场。英伟达Ian Buck在3月发布时即表示：“世界不会由单一SKU的CPU来服务，这也不是我们的意图。”尽管如此，Vera相对当代x86处理器的性能表现证明，英伟达进军独立数据中心CPU并非玩票，其意义远超超大规模厂商此前推出的各类“积木式”Arm芯片，至少足以让AMD和英特尔认真对待。x86阵营的反击即将到来：Zen 6预计年内铺开，英特尔Diamond Rapids瞄准2027年发布。
